Subject: Renewal concessions, co-term strategy, and approval path

Hi team / Sasha,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and attachments: I attached a fresh proposal (frost-uplift-proposal-v2.pdf) and a pricing matrix (redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx). Frost Biotech is evaluating: 1) a mid-contract uplift (~25% more committed usage starting Sep 1), and 2) co-terming this renewal with two other vendor contracts that run to Oct 31.

Customer asks (from Sasha):
- A meaningful uplift discount for the added committed volume (they prefer a single blended uplift price rather than token-by-token tiers)
- Co-term alignment to Oct 31 to simplify procurement
- A billing cadence change (prefer quarterly invoices)

Questions for us:
- What concession structure keeps unit economics intact but meets their approval thresholds?
- Is an SLA-credit alternative viable in lieu of additional off-invoice discount?
- What internal approvals will we need if we go beyond a ~10% headline concession?

Next steps I propose: Ben, can you outline a concession waterfall and a recommended headline? Aditya / Lauren — please flag approvals or legal considerations. Sasha — if you can confirm the expected uplift volume (ballpark ok) and whether Oct 31 co-term is firm, I’ll lock a draft MAP.

Attachments: frost-uplift-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 420 KB); redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB)

Thanks,
Maya

Subject: Re: Renewal concessions, co-term strategy, and approval path

Maya / Sasha —

Thanks — read the attachments. High level recommendation (concession waterfall, preserves revenue while helping procurement sign):

1) Base renewal discount: 7% off list for the renewal term (standard for this segment).
2) Uplift volume rebate: additional 5% applied to the uplifted units if customer commits to annualize the uplift (12-month commit).
3) Co-term incentive: 3% additional if they accept Oct 31 co-term for a 12-month extension instead of a short-term bridge.
4) SLA credit alternative: instead of increasing headline discount, offer an operational SLA credit pool — e.g., up to 2% invoice credit per month for downtime beyond our SLOs, capped at 6% annually. This often satisfies procurement without changing list pricing and preserves renew ARR metrics.

Other considerations:
- If procurement insists on quarterly invoices, we can accommodate but will request a billing admin fee to offset finance ops (nominal).
- Any total concession >12% requires VP revenue approval per our discounts policy.

If Sasha can confirm the uplift % (approx) and whether Oct 31 co-term is mandatory, I’ll prepare the numbers and an approval slide for our revenue ops.

Ben

Thanks Maya/Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround and the SLA-credit suggestion. A few clarifications from our side to make the internal case:

- Uplift sizing: right now we expect the uplift to be ~25% of current committed units starting Sep 1 if we sign by Aug 15. I can confirm exact numbers by Aug 1.
- Co-term: Oct 31 co-term is strongly preferred — consolidates our procurement and reduces contract churn. We could consider a 12-month extension to get the better blended rate if the economics are right.
- Pricing ask: Procurement is pushing for a 15% blended concession on the uplift units to justify the mid-contract change. If you cannot hit that on-list, we are open to a combination: smaller list discount + larger upfront credits (applied as invoice credits) or a prepaid usage bank we can draw from.
- Billing cadence: Quarterly is preferred; we can accept a nominal admin fee if needed.

Forwarding Ben’s bullet points below for internal visibility.

Team —

Quick legal/ops checklist and approval path to keep this moving without surprises: 

- Discount approvals: any net concession >12% (aggregate of list discount + uplift rebate + co-term incentive) requires SVP Revenue sign-off. Prepare a one-slide business case: ARR impact, expected churn reduction, and concession waterfall. I can draft.
- SLA credits: we can structure as an appendix (Operational SLA Credit Addendum). Note: credits that look like penalties require legal review for specific language; we should keep credits limited and tied to measurable SLOs. SOC 2 and audit evidence references must be included if they request monthly credits tied to incident metrics.
- Co-terming: co-terming with other vendor contracts is fine operationally, but procurement wants a single effective date. If Frost wants Oct 31, we need to confirm the transition plan for prorated billing and whether they expect any retroactive credits. Also confirm the effective start for the uplift capacity (Sep 1) vs the co-term date — those can differ but must be explicit in the MAP.
- Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing is OK. Finance requests a billing schedule with PO windows. If they want prepaid usage bank, Finance needs details on draw mechanics and accounting classification.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ben to build a concise concession slide with the waterfall and the ARR math.
2) Maya to draft MAP (mutual action plan) with timelines: internal approval (2–3 business days once Ben provides slide), legal review (3–5 business days), signatures via DocuSign.
3) If the proposed concession exceeds 12%, route to SVP Revenue (Aditya to prep cover memo).

Attachment: discounts-approval-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 45 KB)

I’ll pick this up to draft the MAP once Ben sends the numbers.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Contracts & Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
